next_verification: Compare party congress materials, CPT publications, Thai police/military records and local minority/refugee histories.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Ho Kee Chye’s article reports that the Malayan Communist Party operated from southern Thailand after the first Emergency, experienced an internal factional crisis in the mid-1960s, and announced preparations for southward armed operations in 1968.
confidence: Moderate; this is a short secondary account and no original CPM plenary resolutions were opened.
basis_and_limitations: Ho Kee Chye, Inter-Asia Cultural Studies 16(1), pp.56–66; article discusses the 1961 New Directive, internal split and 1968 statement.
next_verification: Retrieve the CPM New Directive, 1960s Plenum records, 1968 statement and Thai/Malaysian border operational files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Joseph Scalice’s dissertation dates a split in the Philippine PKP to 1967, the founding of the separate Communist Party of the Philippines to 1968, and the establishment of its New People’s Army to 1969.
confidence: Moderate-high for the dated organizational sequence; cross-check founding statements and surviving party records.
basis_and_limitations: Scalice, dissertation chapters 17–21, pp.299–393; full dissertation read.
next_verification: Compare CPP founding congress documents, NPA founding statement, PKP minutes, contemporary newspapers and police files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Scalice argues that the 1965–1966 destruction of the Indonesian PKI influenced the Philippine PKP’s search for new international communist ties and its subsequent alignment within the Sino-Soviet dispute; this is the dissertation author’s causal interpretation.
confidence: High that the dissertation makes this argument; causal weight is not settled and remains the author’s interpretation.
basis_and_limitations: Scalice, abstract and chapter 14, pp.249–260; distinguish documentary sequence from his larger theoretical account.
next_verification: Compare PKP correspondence, Moscow/Beijing records, Indonesian exile networks and other scholarship on the Sino-Soviet split.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Cribb’s 2002 review states that published estimates of deaths in 1965–1966 ranged from 100,000 to two million and that the often-cited 78,000 Fact-Finding Mission figure was recorded while killings were still under way.
confidence: High that the article reports these estimate ranges and timing; the actual death toll remains unresolved.
basis_and_limitations: Cribb, Asian Survey 42(4), pp.557–558. The figures have different dates, methods and institutional purposes.
next_verification: Compare later regional victim lists, Komnas HAM files, provincial registers, demographic studies and the original Fact-Finding Commission report.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Cribb reports that he had found no systematic national collection of survivor, perpetrator and witness testimony suitable for casualty statistics, and that comparison of 1961/1971 census totals by district did not yield a clear excess-loss measure.
confidence: High for what Cribb states; the conclusion is time-bounded and does not establish that no later dataset or unpublished list exists.
basis_and_limitations: Cribb, pp.558–559; he notes only a small number of identified remains and describes national totals as informed estimates.
next_verification: Search post-2002 Komnas HAM, YPKP, local victim databases and burial investigations for ethnicity-coded individual records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Cribb and Coppel’s estimate, as reported in Woolgar’s 2023 article, places ethnic-Chinese deaths in the vicinity of 2,000 against an approximate national total of 500,000; the arithmetic ratio is about 0.4 percent, but neither number is a complete individual count.
claim_type: Secondary casualty estimate and derived ratio
confidence: Low-to-moderate for the estimated count and ratio; high that Woolgar reports Cribb and Coppel's estimate. The 0.4% quotient uses two rounded estimates and is not a measured national proportion.
basis_and_limitations: Woolgar, printed p.1977 and footnote 110, reports Cribb and Coppel’s estimate near 2,000; its footnotes 111–112 discuss the approximate national denominator and cite Cribb and Coppel, 2009, pp.449–450. The denominator is an approximate 500,000 national death estimate and the numerator is an attributed estimate near 2,000. No victim-level ethnic roster supports the quotient; urban/rural and regional variation is substantial.
next_verification: Trace the estimate's underlying provincial reports; seek named victim, burial, community and civil-register data with ethnicity fields. Do not infer national Javanese, Balinese, Sundanese or other group rates from census population shares.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the sources opened for this pass, no national victim-level dataset was found that identifies ethnicity for each person killed; Cribb’s methodological review finds the evidence base inadequate for reliable national ethnic percentages.
confidence: High for the materials reviewed and Cribb’s stated limitation; not proof that such records do not exist elsewhere.
basis_and_limitations: Cribb, pp.557–559; Woolgar, printed p.1977 and footnotes 110–112; Ananta et al. census-method study. The approximate Chinese estimate supplies no Javanese, Balinese, Sundanese or other national breakdown. A 1961 census that omitted ethnicity cannot be combined with non-existent victim-level identities to derive group mortality rates. This is a statement about sources reviewed, not proof no records exist elsewhere.
next_verification: Search Komnas HAM/YPKP person-level records, provincial/village lists, oral-history databases, cemeteries and civil registration; record ethnicity only when the source explicitly supports it.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Woolgar’s West Java study reports that only a few thousand people were killed there in 1965–1966 and that killings of ethnic Chinese appeared rare in that province, contrasting the pattern with northern Sumatra, Medan and Aceh.
confidence: Moderate; regional count and ethnic classification depend on the article’s cited sources, not a complete West Java victim registry.
basis_and_limitations: Woolgar, p.1980, with notes 123–124; the article distinguishes regional patterns and does not claim nationwide uniformity.
next_verification: Retrieve West Java village-level victim lists and compare with North Sumatra, Aceh and Medan records using the same definitions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Woolgar reports that in West Java anti-Chinese harassment and political restrictions continued into 1966, including takeovers of Chinese-language schools and association property, registration measures, pressured name changes and an August 1966 expulsion order affecting some Chinese association members.
claim_type: Regional account of state/civilian discriminatory measures
confidence: Moderate-high for the article’s documented policy/event sequence; individual execution and the scope of each measure require local files.
basis_and_limitations: Woolgar, pp.1980–1981, notes 128–136; these post-purge measures are distinct from deaths during 1965–1966.
next_verification: Read the cited West Java military orders, school/association inventories, registration rolls, deportation records and contemporaneous Chinese-language press.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the 1966 postmortem reproduced by Roosa, Supardjo said the operation’s leadership was divided among Aidit’s group, Sjam’s group and Untung’s group, and argued that operations needed a single command.
confidence: High for the surviving typed text as reproduced and attributed; moderate for the exact structure because the original manuscript is not extant in the examined copy.
basis_and_limitations: Roosa, Dalih Pembunuhan Massal, Appendix 1, pp.323–343; Roosa says the trial-court copy was typed from an original, with possible copying errors.
next_verification: Find Supardjo’s original manuscript, Mahmilub case file and corroborating notes by Untung, Sjam, Soejono and other participants.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Supardjo’s postmortem characterized the plan as a Jakarta “firecracker” expected to ignite popular and regional action, and criticized inadequate verified support, communications and contingency planning.
confidence: High for what the document says; moderate for the operational diagnosis because Supardjo was a participant assigning responsibility after defeat.
basis_and_limitations: Roosa, Appendix 1, pp.328–339; includes Supardjo’s regional courier and command criticism.
next_verification: Compare dated courier routes, provincial instructions, RRI logs, unit movements, party branch reports and the original G30S operation papers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Roosa’s published account of Iskandar Subekti’s confidential 1986 analysis says Aidit met Sjam in August 1965 to discuss a possible action against the alleged Council of Generals, and then approached a small Politburo working group; this is a later participant account mediated through the historian.
claim_type: Retrospective participant account and historian reconstruction
confidence: Moderate; Subekti was an Aidit aide and Politburo note-taker but did not attend Sjam’s meetings with military officers, and the original memo was not independently examined here.
basis_and_limitations: Roosa, chapter 5, pp.150–153; Subekti’s vantage point and limitations are discussed in the text.
next_verification: Locate the 1986 original analysis, compare other working-group members, captured Sjam papers, trial transcripts and contemporaneous calendars.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Subekti’s account, as presented by Roosa, says the Politburo did not meet during September 1965; Roosa infers that the body could not have collectively reviewed Sjam’s detailed operational contacts, but this does not by itself settle what individual leaders knew.
confidence: Moderate for Subekti’s attributed recollection; lower for the inference of complete non-knowledge because original attendance records and parallel communications are absent.
basis_and_limitations: Roosa, pp.150–153; compare Sudisman’s 1967 court defense (S260) and the 1966 party self-criticism (S261).
next_verification: Find September Politburo and Working Committee calendars, minutes, travel/courier records and individual testimony.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Roosa argues that the Army’s official account extended Sjam’s trial testimony from an Aidit-directed operation to a decision by the PKI Central Committee as a whole; this is a historiographical challenge, not an established finding that no other senior figures participated.
claim_type: Historiographical interpretation of official party-responsibility claim
confidence: High that Roosa makes this argument; the underlying level and scope of party authorization remain contested.
basis_and_limitations: Roosa, chapter 5, pp.135–160; compare Sjam’s coercive trial setting, Subekti’s 1986 analysis, Sudisman’s 1967 defense and Supardjo’s 1966 report.
next_verification: Read complete Mahmilub transcripts, original party papers and independent witness accounts; separate individual action, Politburo awareness and formal Central Committee authorization.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A CIA Directorate of Intelligence report in September 1967 discussed the Fifth Force and Sukarno’s health as possible political context but said evidence to confirm its speculation was lacking.
confidence: High for the report’s wording; low for the underlying causal hypotheses.
basis_and_limitations: The indexed passage explicitly characterizes the hypothesis as unconfirmed; the direct PDF request redirected, so only the relevant official OCR excerpt was reviewed.
next_verification: Retrieve the full report scan and compare it with Sukarno’s health records, Indonesian Fifth Force proposals, military memoranda and Chinese records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rewang later stated that the PKI as an institution had not decided to launch the 30 September Movement and recalled that roughly ten Politburo members were confused after it occurred.
confidence: Moderate for what Rewang said; low-to-moderate for a universal negative about all party knowledge.
basis_and_limitations: Liem quotes Rewang’s 2000 interview; no Politburo minutes or signed decision register is available, and Rewang joined the Politburo only in mid-1965.
next_verification: Find the original interview recording/transcript and compare other Politburo members’ notes, calendars and captured party papers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: After Sudisman’s arrest in December 1966, Rewang proposed relocating surviving cadres to a rural base because urban hiding had become unsafe and legal political activity had disappeared.
claim_type: Retrospective participant testimony and scholarly reconstruction
confidence: Moderate; the proposal and motive are reported retrospectively and no recorded vote or directive has been found.
basis_and_limitations: Liem and Hearman rely on Rewang’s later account; the party’s surviving structures were fragmented and this cannot be treated as a nationwide order.
next_verification: Locate Rewang’s original interview, any emergency committee directives and the East Java regional committee’s correspondence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman’s reconstruction identifies at least two surviving leadership groupings, one around Sudisman in Jakarta and another around Ismail Bakri in Bandung, with Rewang aligned with the latter; it does not show one unified underground command.
claim_type: Scholarly reconstruction from participant accounts and later memoirs
confidence: Moderate; the two-group map is a reconstruction and rosters/communications are incomplete.
basis_and_limitations: Hearman, pp.71–74, compares Rewang, Soedjono and Liem accounts; no complete membership list or command archive has been inspected.
next_verification: Find Ismail Bakri’s own papers, each group’s membership and courier lists, and independent reports from regional branches.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem’s interview material describes an emergency Central Committee above provincial leadership and South Blitar project committees; Rewang recalled nine Central Committee members, regional committee figures and cadres from several provinces participating.
confidence: Moderate for the described structure; low for a complete roster, national reach or effective command.
basis_and_limitations: Rewang’s testimony in the chapter’s Kompro section; names, dates and formal authority remain uncorroborated by internal minutes.
next_verification: Obtain the original interview, party rosters, minutes and captured command papers; map each committee’s dates and geographic remit.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A Muyatno interview quoted by Liem describes cells, guerrilla detachments and ideological education, while the article says proposed STPR and KKPR schools were plans; the chapter does not establish that the schools operated as designed.
claim_type: Retrospective testimony and scholarly reconstruction of military materials
confidence: Moderate for the reported plans and testimony; low for implementation at scale.
basis_and_limitations: The article paraphrases documents seized by the Army and survivor accounts; original documents and school attendance lists were not examined.
next_verification: Find the captured files, curriculum, attendance lists, instructor names and evidence of actual training.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Muyatno recalled that Gatot Taryo was the only project-committee contact he knew and also named Joko Untung; he could not identify Joko’s committee role or the wider membership.
confidence: Moderate for the interview’s contents; low for full identities and duties.
basis_and_limitations: The same testimony stresses compartmentalization and limited mutual knowledge; spellings may vary and no personnel records were checked.
next_verification: Search trial files, party lists and local records for Gatot Taryo/Gatot Sutaryo and Joko/Djoko Untung; do not merge variants without identification evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rewang recalled that the start date for a planned armed struggle had not been decided; the emergency leadership expected project preparations and a national conference before authorizing a coordinated campaign.
confidence: Moderate; no minutes confirm the recalled rule or its reach.
basis_and_limitations: The testimony distinguishes preparation of structures from a formal start of organized armed struggle; dispersed cadres may not have followed the same timetable.
next_verification: Find the planned conference agenda, emergency committee resolutions, project reports and regional communications.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem’s interview-based account says some attacks, disarmings and raids occurred outside Kompro decisions and increased military suspicion before the leadership had agreed to begin a coordinated armed struggle.
confidence: Moderate; individual incidents and responsibility require case-by-case corroboration.
basis_and_limitations: Rewang and other participants recall actions the committee had not authorized; Army accounts may describe them differently and no incident roster was checked.
next_verification: Identify each raid, location, date, perpetrators, targets, casualties and arms taken; compare Army logs and local testimony.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Muyatno retrospectively criticized some cadres for seeking quick victory instead of a prolonged Maoist strategy; this is one participant’s diagnosis of internal tactical weakness, not a consensus explanation of PKI’s defeat.
confidence: High that the interviewee made this criticism; moderate-to-low as a general explanation.
basis_and_limitations: Liem quotes Muyatno and Rewang’s related criticism; both were recalling an internal debate after the defeat.
next_verification: Compare dissenting participant accounts, committee papers and the actions each group actually undertook.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem’s interviews describe South Blitar villagers providing housing, food, agricultural work and everyday care to some fugitives; other testimony shows people’s knowledge and participation varied by village and person.
confidence: Moderate for the attributed cases; not generalizable to all residents.
basis_and_limitations: No household roster, village supply ledger or courier register was examined; residents’ assistance could take different forms and need not imply party membership.
next_verification: Locate village-level witness lists, land and household records, food movements, local arrests and independently recorded oral histories.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Leksana’s reconstruction describes early-October 1965 demonstrations, property attacks and clashes in East Java as initially local and uneven, followed from mid-October by more coordinated Army-civilian collaboration.
claim_type: Scholarly reconstruction citing Kodam V Brawijaya records
confidence: Moderate-high for the article’s reconstruction; underlying documents were quoted or summarized rather than opened here.
basis_and_limitations: The article cites East Java military archive collection G30S/PKI tahun 1965, inventory no.316-a. It does not establish uniform enforcement across every district.
next_verification: Inspect inventory 316-a and compare dated orders, district reports, detention registers and local press.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Leksana reports that the East Java commander’s 21 October 1965 Pancasila Operation required battalions to send local-condition reports to Surabaya every six hours and allowed pro-Army civilian forces to assist operations against the September 30 Movement; the instruction was distributed to Korem 081–083 and East Java battalions, with copies sent to Army headquarters, Kostrad, and the Diponegoro and Udayana commands.
claim_type: Scholarly quotation of a contemporaneous military order
confidence: High for the order’s reported language; moderate for actual implementation by each battalion.
basis_and_limitations: The order is quoted from Kodam VIII Brawijaya inventory 316-a through Leksana, not from a signed original reviewed here. Distribution is evidence of intended circulation, not proof that every addressee received, implemented, or reported under it.
next_verification: Obtain the signed Perintah Operasi No. 5 Pantja Sila, its distribution/receipt logs, six-hour situation reports, and unit/auxiliary implementation records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Leksana reports that a 26 October 1965 radiogram placed progressive revolutionary organizations supporting the Army under Puterpra, provided for combative training, and directed district-to-subdistrict investigation teams adapted to local conditions.
claim_type: Scholarly quotation of contemporaneous military radiogram
confidence: High for the article’s account of the radiogram; moderate for implementation and geographic reach.
basis_and_limitations: The account is mediated through Leksana’s reading of inventory 316-a; the original telegram, complete addressees, team composition, and evidence of training or investigation in each locality were not inspected.
next_verification: Obtain Radiogram T. 298/1965, acknowledgements, Puterpra and investigation-team rosters, training attendance, and resulting arrest/interrogation records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Leksana reports that a 23 November 1965 radiogram ordered military-aligned civilian groups to register residents from neighborhood and village levels through districts and institutions, provide information and indoctrination, and assist ABRI operations and psychological-warfare tasks.
claim_type: Scholarly quotation of contemporaneous military radiogram
confidence: High for the provision as quoted; local registration completion is unverified.
basis_and_limitations: The directive is quoted from Brawijaya inventory 316-a through a scholarly article; completion and use of any lists remain unverified. The document's abbreviation AA is not expanded; the author considers an Ansor/religious-group meaning plausible but not certain.
next_verification: Inspect Radiogram T. 702/1965 as cited for 23 November, local registration books, list custodians, handover/use records, and the original order's definition of AA.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Leksana argues that civilian participants in East Java also pursued varied interests, including party competition, revenge and material or employment opportunities; these motives should be tested locally rather than treated as one common civilian motive.
confidence: High that the author advances this analysis; moderate-to-low as a generalization beyond cases documented in the article.
basis_and_limitations: The article’s interpretation does not prove any individual’s motive without local evidence and should be compared with participant testimony and economic records.
next_verification: Compare individual perpetrator accounts, property transfers, hiring lists, party records and village-level disputes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Robinson’s regional comparison argues that military command choices and local capacity produced sharply different outcomes: killings were swift and extensive in Aceh, while West Java’s commander Ibrahim Adjie chose mass arrests rather than similar large-scale killing.
claim_type: Scholarly causal interpretation from regional records
confidence: High that Robinson makes this comparison; moderate as a general causal model and not a rule for all provinces.
basis_and_limitations: The article supports military agency and variation but underlying district records differ and this comparison cannot be universalized to Bali, Java or the archipelago.
next_verification: Compare each province’s force deployment, command continuity, detention and killing records, and civilian auxiliary chain.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Robinson describes KAP-Gestapu as initiated by Army leadership and later covertly assisted financially by the U.S. government; the 2 December Green cable records concurrence with a proposed 50 million rupiah contribution but not a verified transfer or expenditure.
claim_type: Scholarly synthesis compared with contemporaneous U.S. diplomatic record
confidence: High for Robinson’s published interpretation and Green’s documented concurrence; transfer, receipt and use remain unverified.
basis_and_limitations: S175 is a proposal/concurrence with redactions; Robinson’s footnote synthesizes later financial assistance. Do not equate approval intent with proof of cash delivery.
next_verification: Find CIA/State authorization, courier or bank records, Adam Malik receipt, KAP-Gestapu accounts and expenditure evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem reports that military intelligence on South Blitar began by mid-1967, Soeharto issued an operational order on 20 February 1968, and the Trisula task force was formed on 5 May; the chapter cites official effective operations from May through July, while Hearman dates the named operation’s start to June.
claim_type: Scholarly reconstruction with attributed military records
confidence: Moderate-high for the dated stages; the difference between planning, task-force formation and the main field phase requires the original orders.
basis_and_limitations: Liem reports distinct intelligence, cleanup-operation, task-force and effective-attack stages; Hearman’s June date may mark the named field operation rather than all preparation.
next_verification: Read the 20 February order, 5 May formation order, phase reports and 7 September closure record; distinguish phase start from operation name.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem reports an Army announcement that 37 firearms were captured after Trisula; the figure is an Army-reported seizure total and not an independent audit of all party weapons or armed activity.
claim_type: Later scholarly quotation of military operational results
confidence: High for what Liem says the Army announced; low-to-moderate for completeness and accuracy of the total.
basis_and_limitations: Liem reports the Army announced 37 captured firearms; Arief et al.’s 1999 history also attributes the same 37-firearm figure to Yasin’s 9 August 1968 press conference and adds four grenades (printed p.45). These may descend from one official count, not independent corroboration. No physical inventory, post-operation reconciliation or independent arms list was examined.
next_verification: Obtain the Army seizure inventory, unit receipts, prosecution exhibits and any party-side weapons records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem reports that the Army replaced village officials with 234 Army caretakers in South Blitar; the number is attributed to a military source, not a complete appointment roll checked here.
confidence: High for the article’s attributed report; moderate for exact count and locality coverage.
basis_and_limitations: The cited Army monograph and the underlying appointment list were not independently opened.
next_verification: Obtain the 234 names, appointment dates, villages, replacement reasons and local administration files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Ananta and coauthors report that Indonesia did not collect ethnicity in the 1961 census and that the 2000 census was the first post-colonial census to resume it; the 2010 coded data included 1,331 ethnic, sub-ethnic and sub-subethnic categories.
confidence: High for the paper’s methodological account; it says nothing about victim-level ethnicity.
basis_and_limitations: Population census categories and dates cannot supply ethnicity for people killed decades earlier; 2010’s 1,331 raw categories require classification.
next_verification: Find any local civil, cemetery, victim or family roster that records both identity and outcome; document category mapping and missingness.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Cribb and Coppel estimate that approximately 2,000 ethnic-Chinese people were killed in 1965–66, but provide no national victim-level roster; this remains an attributed scholarly estimate and a contested interpretation.
confidence: Moderate for the estimate as a published scholarly position; low-to-moderate for precision because no complete victim list supports it.
basis_and_limitations: Their 2009 article relies partly on earlier work and is polemical in framing; compare Woolgar on West Java and Melvin on Aceh, whose regional evidence can capture different kinds of anti-Chinese violence.
next_verification: Trace the estimate’s underlying sources and compare local ethnic and political identity lists, deaths, disappearances, property attacks and time boundaries.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The ECCC guide summarizes a distinct Cambodian sequence: WPK adopted revolutionary violence in January 1965, ordered zones to prepare armed struggle in September 1966, Samlaut fighting in 1967 arose amid compulsory grain acquisition, and CPK combatants attacked police posts on 17 January 1968.
confidence: High for what the ECCC guide says the Case 002/02 judgment found; moderate as a comparative chronology.
basis_and_limitations: The guide summarizes judgment paragraphs 202–212, not party minutes; the Samlaut conflict’s local actors should not be treated as all centrally directed.
next_verification: Compare the cited judgment paragraphs with Cambodian party documents, village testimony and police records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Zeller argues that the Pathet Lao/Lao People’s Party relied substantially on Vietnamese Workers’ Party cadres and forces, making the Lao armed movement structurally different from the PKI’s national legal mass-party network.
confidence: High that the author advances this interpretation; moderate as a comprehensive description of every Lao unit.
basis_and_limitations: Open-access chapter synthesizes party and external records but is not a full personnel or force census.
next_verification: Compare Lao and Vietnamese party rosters, military orders, supply and command records with Indonesian sources.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Baird’s Hmong-focused CPT study describes recruits entering through basic education and military training, some motivated by schooling and opposition to discrimination, while reporting no Hmong member on the CPT Central Committee and some Hmong provincial-level leadership.
claim_type: Retrospective oral history and social-history comparison
confidence: Moderate; based on a focused group study and extensive retrospective interviews, not a full CPT roster.
basis_and_limitations: Recruitment motives and leadership representation vary by period; the Hmong case cannot stand for all CPT members or be directly mapped onto Indonesian ethnic groups.
next_verification: Compare party membership, training and leadership records for other CPT constituencies and assess the interview sample.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The combined evidence supports testing two distinct causal layers: PKI’s leadership concentration, reliance on a small officer-contact network and weak clandestine contingency planning may help explain G30S operational failure and post-purge vulnerability, while Army command, state detention and killing machinery, civilian collaboration and external support belong to the separate mechanisms that destroyed the party’s mass organizations.
claim_type: Analytical synthesis; causal hypothesis, not authorial political judgment
confidence: Moderate as a framework for testing; causal weight and political evaluation remain unsettled.
basis_and_limitations: Evidence describes distinct processes and sources have differing vantage points; this does not establish a single internal PKI cause for mass killing or assign the author’s final political position.
next_verification: Build province-by-province process tracing from orders, unit logs, victim records, party communications, property changes and foreign-operation chains.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem’s retrospective chapter says the PKI had no party-led armed-struggle plan before G30S and operated through the existing political system; after the party was banned and its leaders and members were attacked, Sudisman shifted the surviving party toward an armed-resistance strategy during 1966.
claim_type: Scholarly reconstruction based on participant interviews and attributed party/military accounts
confidence: Moderate for Liem’s reconstruction; not proof that no individual or affiliated group held military ideas or training.
basis_and_limitations: Liem, opening section and South Blitar narrative, says pre-G30S the party had no plan to launch armed struggle, remained close to Sukarno and worked within existing politics, then describes Sudisman’s 1966 shift after repression. This must be distinguished from the Fifth Force debate, volunteer training, BTI/HANREV activities, veterans in party networks and post-1965 planned resistance; contemporary party records remain to be checked.
next_verification: Compare 1964–65 PKI/BTI/Gerwani/Fifth Force documents and military training records with Sudisman’s 1966 self-criticism, internal directives, provincial files and later exile correspondence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a 1963 public report, Aidit retrospectively described the 1950–51 debate between immediate armed struggle and rebuilding the party while preserving its legal status; he said the party chose the latter after judging its organization weak and the revolutionary situation ebbing.
confidence: High for what Aidit stated; moderate as a complete account of the internal debate
basis_and_limitations: Aidit’s programmatic report is an interested account defending the post-1951 line; it is not a transcript of all Central Committee debate.
next_verification: Compare the 1951 CC minutes, rival-line documents, membership and branch reports, and Madiun-era security records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Aidit’s 1963 report says the 1951 reconstruction used Central Committee-appointed provincial commissariats because local organizations were confused, while inter-island communications and transport remained a serious problem.
confidence: High for the report’s statement; moderate for nationwide implementation and scale
basis_and_limitations: The text explains the party’s chosen central-supervision structure and explicitly notes the archipelago communications problem; no provincial reports were independently checked.
next_verification: Retrieve appointment, courier, travel, transport, membership and provincial committee records for multiple islands.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Aidit’s 1963 report publicly called for links between the armed forces and the people and used the “rifle in one hand, hoe in the other” slogan; this is evidence of militarized political language and a mass-line conception, not proof of a PKI field army, weapons delivery or combat order.
claim_type: Party programmatic text; distinction between rhetoric and capability
confidence: High for published language and catalogue descriptions; low for any inferred force capability
basis_and_limitations: Aidit’s text is not an operational order. ANRI entries 257–259 remain catalogue locators only, and participant accounts describe a limited post-1965 underground project.
next_verification: Read BTI items 257–259 and HANREV files; identify participants, instructors, chain of command, weapons and actual use.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The September 1966 Politburo self-criticism says party leaders involved themselves in the 30 September Movement without organizational procedure or a mass base, calls this adventurism, and says the leadership then entrusted the party’s fate to Sukarno after the movement failed.
confidence: High that the document says this; moderate-to-low as an independently verified causal diagnosis
basis_and_limitations: The text itself says the Politburo bore greatest responsibility, but was produced under military terror after severe leadership losses and as the surviving group redirected party strategy. It does not specify which individuals approved what in September 1965.
next_verification: Compare drafting and circulation records, surviving leaders’ criticism, Sudisman’s 1967 defense, Rewang interviews, Supardjo’s report, Subekti’s analysis and contemporaneous party minutes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1966 self-criticism attributes past organizational weakness to the leadership’s failure to develop criticism/self-criticism, its reported suppression of criticism from below, and an overly loose, legalistic mass-party structure.
confidence: High for the document’s diagnosis; moderate for the history it describes
basis_and_limitations: This diagnosis is a politically situated post-defeat text advocating a new Maoist armed line; independent party records and survivor accounts are needed to test whether these weaknesses were uniform and decisive.
next_verification: Find party education and discipline records, cadre evaluations, recruitment statistics, internal criticism, provincial security plans and communications.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The September 1966 self-criticism says the pre-1965 “three forms of struggle”—rural guerrilla activity, urban worker action and work among armed forces—were separated and pursued along a peaceful route, effectively abandoning armed struggle; the statement presents this as a failure, not a contemporaneous operational description.

confidence: High for the later document’s wording; contested as a description of actual practice

next_verification: Compare 1956, 1959, 1962–65 party congress resolutions, armed-forces committees, BTI training files and local branch implementation.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Woolgar’s 2025 study characterizes the PKI as a hybrid of cadre/vanguard party, mass party and social movement: growth increased bureaucratic hierarchy while also producing a looser, less coherent organization.
period: 1951–1965, with West Java as the case study

basis_and_limitations: Based on the author’s stated use of party/KOTI archives, publications and oral histories; only the accepted introduction was read, not the full monograph or underlying files.
next_verification: Read the full chapters on Guided Democracy, mass organizations and destruction; compare with Central/East Java, Bali, Sumatra, Sulawesi and party rosters.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Woolgar argues that fast growth and attempted central control did not eliminate local differentiation: in West Java the party faced an entrenched Siliwangi military presence and increasing opposition, while provincial events could exceed leaders’ control.
confidence: Moderate; West Java evidence is stronger than any nationwide inference

next_verification: Inspect the book’s source notes and compare district-level party/military records from other provinces.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Woolgar interprets the leadership’s post-October 1965 paralysis as a combination of shock and strategic miscalculation that exposed the vulnerability of the mass membership; he links this to unresolved tensions between mass-party, movement and vanguard roles.

basis_and_limitations: The source is a West Java-centered monograph whose introduction summarizes a broader chapter; mass killing and detention were actions of state and military actors and are separate from PKI organizational vulnerability.
next_verification: Compare central and provincial leadership responses, military orders, arrests, killings and communications with time-stamped local records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Komnas HAM’s report gives at least 1,956 witness-based victims in the legal category “murder” and at least 85,483 in the distinct category “extermination”; it does not present these as a complete national death census or disaggregate them by ethnicity.

confidence: High for the report’s categories and figures; low as a national total
basis_and_limitations: The report’s legal categories use witness statements and cover multiple regions; its own methodology says the team examined 349 people but could not investigate every region or witness because of geographic scope, budget and the passage of time. Other violation categories may overlap, so counts must not be summed into one victim total. No national ethnicity table or ethnic denominator was found; underlying BAPs remain unopened.
next_verification: Inspect underlying witness BAPs and regional annexes; determine geographic coverage, duplicate handling, category definitions and whether any victim records contain ethnicity fields. Do not convert the “extermination” category into a death count or derive ethnic percentages without person-level records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Komnas HAM records that October 1965 attacks in Makassar targeted alleged PKI-linked people and ethnic-Chinese residents who were perceived as connected to the PRC; it supplies no count that can produce an ethnic share of nationwide deaths.
claim_type: Official report of witness-based local violence

basis_and_limitations: The report describes local crowd attacks, looting and destruction but does not provide a complete Makassar or national ethnicity-coded victim list.
next_verification: Read the cited BAPs, local police/military records, Chinese association records, and burial or civil registers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The approximately 2,000 ethnic-Chinese deaths estimate divided by an approximately 500,000 overall estimate yields about 0.4% arithmetically, but this is not a measured victim share and cannot establish comparative ethnic risk; reliable national percentages for other groups were not found.
claim_type: Derived arithmetic from contested scholarly estimates; data-gap finding
confidence: High that the ratio is only derived from approximate estimates; very low as a measured population statistic
basis_and_limitations: Neither numerator nor denominator is a complete individual-level roster with matched ethnic identity, geography and period. The 1961 census did not collect ethnicity; post-2000 census data do not fill a 1965 victim roster.
next_verification: Locate and de-duplicate provincial/village victim registers and identify whether ethnicity is recorded; calculate only for defined samples with denominators.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The South Kelud study reports that about 515 Gambar residents petitioned to legalize cultivation of roughly 196 hectares; the figure is the study’s report of a local petition, not an independently checked land registry.

confidence: Moderate for the reported petition; unverified as a completed land transfer

atomic_claim_or_observation: The South Kelud study reports that 365 households were evicted from plantation land after 1965, with homes dismantled and little compensation; this is a local article’s account, not a verified national total.

next_verification: Find the cited 1980s newspaper reports, eviction orders, household lists, compensation files and land concession records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In Constitutional Court case 55/PUU-VIII/2010, farmer Sakri from Soso, Blitar, asserted that he cultivated state land formerly under an erfpacht controlled by PT Kismo Handayani and relied on SK49/KA/64; the judgment also reproduces the government’s account of a July 2008 demonstration and Sakri’s suspended sentence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman’s South Blitar study describes military evacuation, camps, village surveillance and food scarcity during the 1968 counterinsurgency; villagers were pressured to assist with food, patrol or control, and accounts vary by locality.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The source combination supports a bounded explanation of PKI military weakness: armed rhetoric, contacts, training proposals and some training do not by themselves prove a centralized guerrilla army; leadership decision structure, communications, command failure, Army territorial power and the later destruction of mass organizations must be tested as separate mechanisms.
claim_type: Cross-source analytical proposition for later testing
confidence: Moderate as a research model; no single source establishes the whole chain
basis_and_limitations: Aidit is a party text, the BTI inventory is a finding aid, self-criticism is post-defeat, underground accounts are retrospective, and Army power varies by province. It is not a final political judgment or single-cause verdict.
next_verification: Build province-by-province maps of PKI armed assets, Army territorial units, civilian mobilization, arrests, killings and links between written orders and implementation.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Chandra’s East Java estimate of one-time district-level population change compares census-based expected population with later observed counts; it combines deaths above normal, lower fertility and one-time migration, so it is a proxy for disruption rather than a direct death count.

basis_and_limitations: The study is East Java-specific and depends on population-growth assumptions and changing district boundaries.
next_verification: Compare the 491 district estimates with local victim registers, burial evidence, migration testimony and boundary harmonization; do not label the proxy “deaths.”

confidence: Moderate for the reported association; not proof of a specific killing operation
basis_and_limitations: The measure uses a 1971 main-road map, excludes minor roads and other transport, and population change also includes fertility and migration. Correlation does not by itself show army or civilian action in a particular district.
next_verification: Match road accessibility to dated transport orders, truck logs, detention/transfer records, local testimony and mass-grave evidence by district.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Chandra and Zhang’s 2023 abstract says their East Java spatial analysis compares kecamatan population-loss estimates with Army command-center and politico-religious organization-center locations and identifies possible military/civilian-allied hotspots; the authors state the model cannot prove any named group or individual took part.

basis_and_limitations: The full paper and model specification were not accessed. Population-loss proxy is not a victim list; locations of institutions do not establish operational control.
next_verification: Read full paper, maps, robustness checks, organization lists and citations; compare each hotspot with primary local orders, personnel and testimony.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman’s account of Rewang’s testimony frames South Blitar primarily as a refuge from persecution; Rewang assessed organized armed resistance after 1966 as negligible, and only one detachment of young men had received training by the 1968 Trisula operation.

next_verification: Read Rewang’s 2017 memoir and full interview recordings; obtain Kompro rosters, training attendance, weapons and operation records, and local testimony.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The Ministry of Home Affairs library catalog identifies a 2017 Indonesian-language book Saya Seorang Revolusioner and says it contains Rewang testimony on G30S, South Blitar and the Politburo self-criticism’s formation; the catalog is a lead to a participant source, not evidence of the testimony’s exact content.

basis_and_limitations: The actual book was not read; catalog metadata does not establish whether Rewang was interviewed directly, how the text was edited, or the statement’s date and completeness.
next_verification: Acquire the book; record edition, editor/interviewer, chapter/page references, interview dates, and textual differences against Liem and Hearman.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Woolgar’s West Java study repeats the Cribb–Coppel estimate of about 2,000 ethnic-Chinese deaths and argues they were not nationally overrepresented relative to an approximate 500,000 death estimate and roughly 2% population share; it also documents regional variation and anti-Chinese harassment, detention, property attacks and expulsions.

confidence: Moderate as a published interpretation; not a measured national victim-ethnicity share
basis_and_limitations: There is no national victim-level ethnic roster in these sources; the denominator and numerator are approximate, and region-specific experiences differ. “Not disproportionately represented” does not mean no anti-Chinese targeting or no local overrepresentation.
next_verification: Trace the estimate’s underlying records and compare regionally bounded ethnic victim lists, population denominators, deaths, detention and expulsion separately.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Winward’s Yogyakarta reconstruction places Suharto’s announcement of Kopkamtib on 10 October 1965 as a parallel security command, RPKAD deployment to Central Java on 17 October, and RPKAD arrival in Yogyakarta on 20 October; this is a scholarly chronology, not a substitute for the underlying orders.

next_verification: Retrieve UGM and other institutional purge orders, original lists, military intake files and individual case records; compare names and outcomes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Winward reports that RPKAD and military police selected ten civilians, armed them and authorized them to lead auxiliary units, with legal-immunity assurances described by one interviewee; this is a localized account of state-enabled militia formation, not a nationwide militia count.
claim_type: Retrospective participant account within a scholarly case study
confidence: Moderate for the attributed Yogyakarta account; low for numerical generalization
basis_and_limitations: The statement relies on a former militia leader’s confidential interview; weapon issue and legal guarantees have not been matched to official records.
next_verification: Find the auxiliary-unit roster, training and arms receipts, appointment/protection orders, and comparison with East Java and other regions.

claim_type: Scholarly causal interpretation of civil–military relations
confidence: Moderate as a bounded case interpretation; national generalization requires provincial evidence
basis_and_limitations: Interviews and military accounts support the process reconstruction, but sample is nonrepresentative and actors’ memories or self-presentation may be selective. Army custody of detainees and transport/organization remain distinct from militia violence outside authorization.
next_verification: Compare provincial orders, local force loyalties, detention/execution pathways, militia links and stop/discipline directives.

period: 1965–1966; Central Java, with West/East Java comparison
claim_type: Published analytical hypothesis and disclosed methodological caveats
confidence: Moderate that this is the author’s stated mechanism; causal strength unassessed without full article
basis_and_limitations: Only abstract and appendices were accessed. Census-based district change in S1332 mixes death, fertility and migration; the interview sample is not statistically representative; individual orders and local records need verification.
next_verification: Read full article and appendix-linked source trail; test district-by-district against command orders, prison capacity, lists, military units and local victim evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Winward contrasts Yogyakarta’s weaker pre-existing militia networks and lack of a large-scale land-reform campaign with East Java’s denser pesantren/Ansor-Banser networks and sharper local agrarian conflicts; despite those differences, Yogyakarta violence escalated after RPKAD deployment and civilian-military coordination.
confidence: Moderate as a comparison to test; not a claim that Yogyakarta had no local disputes or that East Java was uniform
basis_and_limitations: Winward notes small isolated land disputes in Yogyakarta; regional comparisons are qualitative and categories such as “militia network” and “land conflict” need localized measurement.
next_verification: Compare district-level pre-1965 land actions, party strength, armed-unit loyalties, civilian organization rosters and violence timing in Yogyakarta, Central/East/West Java.

basis_and_limitations: The account appears in a courtroom defense and casts the purpose as opposing a Council of Generals coup; no meeting record or military participants are identified by name.
next_verification: Search East Java Special Bureau records, Rustomo/Suwandi files, military-unit logs and trial testimony.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Munir argued that Biro Chusus was an Aidit-created parallel channel absent from the PKI constitution and not reported to ordinary party committees.
claim_type: Retrospective institutional claim in a legal defense
confidence: High that Munir made this argument; medium that it accurately captures formal constitutional status
basis_and_limitations: The statement is self-defensive and should be compared with 1966 self-criticism, party documents, officers' accounts and evidence of actual operating practice.
next_verification: Locate the PKI constitution editions, Bureau rosters, reporting lines, correspondence and original trial evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Munir described the post-1966 South Blitar relocation as an effort to rebuild an illegal party from rural bases and shelter members and their families from pursuit and violence.
claim_type: Retrospective participant account of motive and organization
confidence: High that the plea states this rationale; medium for its representativeness across the whole network
basis_and_limitations: Munir's account presents his own and the leadership's stated purpose; it does not show that all local activity followed a single plan.
next_verification: Compare Rewang and other survivor interviews, village records, military operational histories and party correspondence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Munir said South Blitar had not yet met the three conditions he considered necessary to begin an armed revolution: a strong party, broad mass support, and a workers' and peasants' revolutionary army.
confidence: High that this was Munir's assessment in the plea; medium for the condition of every local unit
basis_and_limitations: A defense argument after capture is not a neutral force audit; it is consistent with but not identical to other testimony that training and arms remained limited.
next_verification: Find membership and village-support lists, training rosters, weapon inventories and records of armed actions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Munir said South Blitar had village guerrilla militias and semi-regular guerrilla detachments, but no People's Liberation Army (TPR).
confidence: High that the plea says this; medium for exact strength and organization
basis_and_limitations: No roster, command chart or unit inventory accompanies the statement; it uses Munir's own terminology in a legal defense.
next_verification: Compare the original plea with Trisula reports, regional military records, participant accounts and captured-document inventories.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Munir reported that Army operations in South Blitar began in January 1968, that the Politburo chose defensive resistance and escape from encirclement in April, and that the base fell in August.
confidence: High that the plea gives these dates; medium for the chronology of operations
basis_and_limitations: His January–August sequence may refer to a wider period of encirclement and local operations, not the named Trisula campaign, which Hearman dates from June; do not merge the two labels.
next_verification: Obtain the plea original, army operational orders, Trisula chronology, provincial command logs and village-level records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Munir attributed South Blitar's defeat partly to leadership rebuilding too hastily and exposing activity before preparations were mature, and partly to the Army attacking with overwhelming force.
confidence: High that Munir offered this explanation; medium that haste and exposure contributed; low as a complete causal account
basis_and_limitations: Munir was a captured defendant and Hearman's account draws partly on overlapping survivor testimony; neither alone measures the relative cause of defeat.
next_verification: Compare independent local testimony, captured correspondence, Army intelligence and operation files, food/arms records and arrest chronology.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the reproduced plea Munir presented a post-1966 'three-banner' line centered on rebuilding a Leninist party, armed people's struggle led by workers and peasants, and a revolutionary united front.
confidence: High that Munir stated this line in the plea; medium as a description of the broader party position
basis_and_limitations: The speech is an individual leader's retrospective exposition; it must be checked against the original 1966 Politburo self-criticism and other survivor groups' programs.
next_verification: Compare the 1966 self-criticism manuscript, surviving party pamphlets, regional instructions and contemporaneous underground documents.

atomic_claim_or_observation: TAPOL reported in 1982 that Munir was SOBSI General Secretary and Ruslan deputy General Secretary at the time the federation was banned, while describing Munir as deputy General Secretary from 1952.
confidence: High that TAPOL printed these titles and career dates; medium for the exact office chronology
basis_and_limitations: Hearman 2016 and 2024 use different translated titles and describe different dates/offices. The discrepancy may reflect rank changes over time or terminology; it should not be silently harmonized.
next_verification: Check SOBSI congress proceedings, executive rosters, Indonesian union newspapers and WFTU records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: TAPOL reported that Mohammad Munir was born in Madura in 1925.
confidence: High that TAPOL reports this; medium as an exact birth year
basis_and_limitations: No civil registration or family record was checked.

atomic_claim_or_observation: TAPOL reported that Munir began full-time SOBSI work in 1950 and became a deputy General Secretary in 1952.
confidence: High that TAPOL reports these dates; medium for exact appointment chronology

next_verification: Check SOBSI congress and executive records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that Munir was a WFTU General Council member and Ruslan a SOBSI deputy secretary-general/WFTU General Council member; her 2016 article uses a different SOBSI rank for Ruslan than her 2024 article.
confidence: High that the articles report these distinctions; medium for exact rank-and-date reconciliation
