atomic_claim_or_observation: The decree’s preamble says the book contained writings and accusations attacking the personal character of Indonesia’s national leader/President and could disturb public order; it cites an opinion from the head of BAKIN dated 11 April 1986, no. R/921/IV/1986/G.
claim_type: Official decision text, visually checked scan
confidence: High that this is the decision’s stated basis; the underlying BAKIN opinion and the accuracy of the decree’s characterization have not been independently examined.
basis_and_limitations: The asserted threat and attack are the government’s own legal characterization, not a neutral evaluation of the book’s arguments. The named intelligence opinion is referenced but unavailable in this pass.
next_verification: Obtain BAKIN opinion R/921/IV/1986/G, compare it with the full book and related Attorney General decisions, and look for internal circulation instructions.

atomic_claim_or_observation: KEP-044/J.A/6/1986, dated 18 June 1986, prohibits circulation of Harold Crouch’s Militer dan Politik di Indonesia, orders persons holding or distributing copies to surrender them, and authorizes prosecutors, police or other public-order agencies to seize them. Its preamble says the book may harm the national interest and cause public distrust of national leadership and government; it cites a Department of Information recommendation of 9 May 1986, No.268/IJ/K/V/RHS/1986.
claim_type: Official legal order; visually checked scan
confidence: High for the decree’s text and stated rationale; no independent assessment of the book or implementation.
basis_and_limitations: The cited recommendation is not included in the scan. The legal order documents the government’s action and justification, not the recommendation’s drafting process, its evidentiary basis, or actual nationwide enforcement.
next_verification: Obtain the Department of Information recommendation, Attorney General file, local seizure reports, publisher correspondence and customs/postal records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: ELSAM’s 1999 study reports that in June 1986 a House Commission I hearing with BAKIN included Vice Chair Rusli Desa urging a ban on Harold Crouch’s book, arguing it would undermine public trust in the President. ELSAM says the ban followed “a month later”; the official KEP-044 order is dated 18 June 1986, and the study gives no hearing day, so the stated interval cannot be independently reconciled and may be approximate.
claim_type: Retrospective secondary account contrasted with official order date
confidence: High that ELSAM reports the hearing and JDIH dates the order 18 June; low for the exact interval and the hearing’s causal weight.
basis_and_limitations: No hearing minutes, transcript, attendee list, or Rusli Desa statement was obtained. The hearing, BAKIN’s institutional attendance, and the separate formal recommendation cited by the decree must not be collapsed into one proven decision chain.
next_verification: Obtain Commission I minutes/audio, BAKIN hearing records, the 9 May Department of Information recommendation, and the full Attorney General review file.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Penetapan Presiden No.4/1963 authorized the Minister/Attorney General to prohibit printed matter deemed disruptive of public order; provided for seizure by prosecutors, police or other authorized public-order agencies; allowed prior screening of selected imported printed matter and return of banned foreign material held by postal offices; and required a printer to submit one copy within 48 hours for the listed classes of printed matter.
period: 1963 onward; invoked in the 1986 KEP-041 and KEP-044 orders
claim_type: Primary legislation and later invocation in official orders
confidence: High for the statutory text and its citation in the two 1986 orders; actual enforcement practice remains case-specific.
basis_and_limitations: The statute sets legal powers and procedures, not proof that every imported item was screened, every copy surrendered, or each local office complied.
next_verification: Compare implementation files, State Gazette notices, import/customs and postal records, and local prosecutor/police inventories for the 1985 Amsterdam book.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1963 decree’s preamble describes foreign influence delivered through imported printed matter as a matter the government should control; its explanatory note gives harm to belief in the revolution, socialism and national leadership as examples of “disturbing public order,” leaving the assessment to the Minister/Attorney General.
claim_type: Primary legal text and official explanation
confidence: High that this was the decree’s stated ideological and legal rationale.
basis_and_limitations: This is the Sukarno-era legal text and explanation, not evidence by itself of the motives behind either 1986 ban or of actual foreign operations.
next_verification: Read in parallel with the specific 1986 order preambles and the underlying BAKIN/Department of Information recommendations.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Jaringan Kerja Budaya/ELSAM reports that New Order book-ban proposals also came from other government bodies and social organizations; that routine political-security coordination meetings chaired by Menko Polkam included the Attorney General and senior government/military officials; and that BAKIN, Bakorstanas, Bais ABRI, Polri and the Ministry of Religion sent views to the Attorney General, while the Attorney General’s intelligence deputy gathered information on “sensitive” books.
claim_type: Secondary institutional reconstruction citing decrees and ban-order recitals
confidence: High that the book makes this account; moderate as a reconstruction of recurring administrative practice pending primary minutes and correspondence.
basis_and_limitations: No meeting minutes, submission letters, intelligence files or staffing records were inspected. The listed agencies did not necessarily participate in every individual ban; keep each order’s named inputs separate.
next_verification: Acquire Menko Polkam meeting records, institutional letters attached to individual ban cases, Attorney General intelligence files and underlying records cited in ELSAM’s footnotes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Keppres No.10/1986 formally defines Muspida as a consultation/coordination forum linking regional governments, ABRI officers and other state apparatus; it tasks the forum with coordinating regional agencies, assessing disturbances to public order and determining prevention/response measures. Its provincial and district membership includes regional executives, military commanders, police chiefs and prosecutors; it also replaces Inpres No.05/1967.
claim_type: Primary presidential decree, full text reviewed
confidence: High for the decree’s text and date.
basis_and_limitations: A formal framework does not prove a particular meeting addressed books or that local prosecutors acted before a national order. The arrangement predates the 1986 decree in earlier form.
next_verification: Locate provincial and district Muspida minutes and follow-up orders, including cases involving circulation of books and printed materials.

atomic_claim_or_observation: ELSAM reports that local Muspida forums discussed circulation of books labeled dangerous as a security concern, and that local prosecutors sometimes acted on this basis before an Attorney General decision.
claim_type: Secondary account of local enforcement practice
confidence: High that ELSAM reports this practice; low to moderate for prevalence and exact cases absent local files.
basis_and_limitations: The decree defines Muspida’s mandate but not this book-specific practice. No particular Muspida minutes, local seizure record or dated pre-national action was obtained.
next_verification: Find district/provincial meeting minutes, local prosecutor decisions, police inventories and bookshop/publisher records for named cases in ELSAM’s pp.35–36.

atomic_claim_or_observation: ELSAM says Bakorstanas replaced Kopkamtib under Keppres 29/1988 and that a cross-agency book-review “clearing house” was formally established under Attorney General decision KEP-114/JA/10/1989 with 19 members. This formalized later review arrangements but came after the June 1986 KEP-041 and KEP-044 bans and cannot explain their procedure.
claim_type: Retrospective institutional account; primary decision not inspected
confidence: High that ELSAM reports this sequence; details of the 1989 body await primary-document verification.
basis_and_limitations: The 1989 clearing house must not be projected backward as the formal procedure for the 1986 bans. No signed KEP-114/JA/10/1989 or Bakorstanas founding order was obtained.
next_verification: Obtain Keppres 29/1988 and KEP-114/JA/10/1989, membership lists, meeting minutes and case-review records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The official June 1986 orders name different administrative inputs: KEP-041 for the Amsterdam book cites a BAKIN chief opinion dated 11 April 1986, while KEP-044 for Crouch’s book cites a Department of Information recommendation dated 9 May 1986. This establishes multiple formal channels named in the orders, not the relative influence or full informal process behind either decision.
claim_type: Cross-reading of two official decision scans
confidence: High for the inputs each decree names; low for the causal role and informal contacts.
basis_and_limitations: The underlying BAKIN and Department of Information memoranda, any associated security-coordination minutes and their evidence have not been obtained.
next_verification: Request both cited memoranda and trace their routing, attachments, recipients, review notes and implementation records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that former political prisoners smuggled copies of Gatot Lestario’s 26 December 1975 courtroom defense speech out of prison; she says it was later translated into Dutch, introduced by W.F. Wertheim, published in a booklet on the 1965–1966 abuses and retitled Indonesië klaagt aan in explicit reference to Sukarno’s 1930 defense.
claim_type: Peer-reviewed retrospective account based on letters, archival materials and interviews
confidence: High that Hearman’s article makes this account; moderate pending inspection of the Dutch booklet and the smuggling/translation records.
basis_and_limitations: The 1985 Dutch booklet and underlying custody/transfer records were not inspected. The article’s wording does not settle whether the phrase is a separate title page, a heading for the plea, or an editorial retitling within the larger book.
next_verification: Inspect the full Stichting Indonesia Media book and compare title leaf, contents, plea heading, translator/editor notes, page span, source manuscript and cited interviews.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Indonesië klaagt aan is also the alternate Dutch title recorded for a separate 1985 Indonesian-language edition of Sukarno’s defense Indonesia menggugat; CiNii identifies Sukarno as author and records 188 pages and three library holdings. This supports a title collision and does not identify Lestario’s plea as the same work.
claim_type: Union-catalog bibliographic distinction cross-checked against later scholarly account
confidence: High for the CiNii bibliographic record; moderate for Hearman’s stated deliberate allusion until the Lestario booklet is inspected.
basis_and_limitations: The CiNii entry describes a separate Sukarno edition; it does not describe the title page or contents of Lestario’s Dutch plea.
next_verification: Compare both physical publications; record publisher, title leaf, contents, pagination and whether Indonesië klaagt aan appears as title, heading or subtitle in the Lestario volume.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A specialist private bibliography lists Gatot Lestario’s plea within the 1985 booklet with W.F. Wertheim and Peter Dale Scott; an antiquarian dealer lists that same title but gives 35 pages, while Scott’s bibliography places his essay within it at pp.170–235. The page-count descriptions conflict and do not establish the actual length of the Lestario plea or edition.
claim_type: Bibliographic discrepancy across catalog/finding-aid and sales listing
confidence: High that the listings conflict; low for which pagination statement or edition is correct until a copy is inspected.
basis_and_limitations: Peter Schumacher’s direct page timed out and only its indexed text was available; Ardjoeno is a bookseller listing. Scott is a contributor and his own retrospective bibliography is not a physical-copy inspection.
next_verification: Locate a library or private copy; photograph title leaf, contents, colophon, and pages 1–235; determine whether different editions or separate pamphlets share the title.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a separate March 2001 interview, Maryono told André Liem that soldiers brought roughly forty men to the Ngrejo riverside and shot them; he recalled eight returned to a cave and thirty-two buried in two pits, named several victims from memory, and said he did not know whether the victims were PKI or BTI members.
period: 1968; Ngrejo / South Blitar, precise site unresolved
claim_type: Retrospective local witness testimony recorded in an oral-history chapter
confidence: High that the 2004 chapter records this separate interview; medium for the episode details and identities.
basis_and_limitations: Printed pp.196–199; Maryono says “if I am not mistaken” about forty. He recalls Sani, Senen Parjono, Wagimin, Suro Kempleng, Gentong, Kamto and Sonto, but names are not cross-checked against civil or party records. Liem’s interview list dates Maryono to March 2001. This is a second retrospective witness within the same project as Paijo, not a contemporaneous independent record.
next_verification: Find the audio/transcript, confirm place-name variants and burial/cave site, seek relatives and missing-person registers, and compare with military transport/death/detention logs and archaeological evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A Blitar resident identified in Liem’s chapter as Harsono recalled that Chinese residents of Blitar city were assembled at Dipoyono cinema and told to support the authorities, especially the military, with money; he said vehicles were borrowed for operations and residents felt business and safety depended on contributions to Kodim.
period: After October 1965; Blitar city, exact date and duration unspecified
claim_type: Retrospective ethnic-minority testimony quoted through a later oral-history chapter
confidence: High that Liem reproduces the account; low-to-moderate for the full scope and implementation absent other witnesses or records.
basis_and_limitations: Printed pp.173–174 and footnote citing Jaringan Kerja Budaya, Kumpulan Hasil Diskusi Tahun 2000, pp.128–129; the underlying discussion volume, meeting recording, summons, receipts and vehicle logs were not separately inspected. Harsono says he was not a Baperki member. One account cannot establish a national policy, an exact number of people or payments, or that every Blitar Chinese resident complied.
next_verification: Locate the cited 2000 discussion volume and recording; identify Harsono and the meeting date; seek Kodim transport/fund accounts, business records and independent Blitar Chinese families’ testimony.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that PKI members with agricultural training tried to share cultivation knowledge with South Blitar villagers and improve yields or diversify crops, including techniques suited to local soil and food conditions.
claim_type: Secondary synthesis of retrospective accounts and agricultural/military materials
confidence: High that Hearman reports these activities; medium-to-low for their reach and results.
basis_and_limitations: Printed pp.86–89; the article describes agricultural technicians and education in soil/fertilizer, crops and production. It is not an audited program list; no village-by-village participant roster, crop plot records or yield series were inspected. It does not establish that all projects were voluntary or that every cadre shared one approach.
next_verification: Inspect the article’s cited Rewang and Lies Sari sources, agricultural project and village records, crop/land data and testimony from participating and nonparticipating farmers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that military intelligence, relying on information from local NU allies, alleged that PKI fugitives compelled villagers to grow and supply food as a form of “taxation.”
claim_type: Security allegation as reported in later scholarship
confidence: High that Hearman reports the allegation; low that coercive taxation occurred as described.
basis_and_limitations: Printed p.90 and note 45. The article attributes the information to military intelligence and local NU allies, not a directly identified household witness or contemporaneous tax register. Crop-extension efforts and food-provisioning work are also documented; this allegation cannot be used to characterize them all as forced extraction.
next_verification: Find the underlying military intelligence report and named sources; compare village testimony, crop transfers, party instructions, food ledgers and evidence of coercion or voluntary exchange.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman says Brawijaya commander Muhammad Jasin told the East Java regional parliament that a reforestation project existed in South Blitar under BTI leader Djadi Wirjosubroto.
period: 1967–1968; South Blitar / East Java regional parliament
claim_type: Later scholarly report of a military commander’s parliamentary statement
confidence: High that the article reports the statement; medium for its exact wording and project details.
basis_and_limitations: Printed p.90 and note 46. The parliament transcript and referenced military report were not obtained. This establishes what Hearman says Jasin reported, not the project’s full size, coercion, outputs or village participation.
next_verification: Obtain East Java parliament minutes and the cited Brawijaya file; identify project dates, leadership, sites, labor terms and relation to pre-1965 BTI agricultural programs.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that during the 1968 operation villages were evacuated and residents held in camps such as Bakung to obstruct food reaching fugitives; a pseudonymous witness, Zainab, recalled that despite promised camp kitchens and field hospitals residents had to bring their own food and became hungry enough to eat raw sweet potatoes and other crops.
claim_type: Oral-history testimony and later historian’s reconstruction
confidence: High that the article records the account and gives this explanation of camp policy; medium for details pending camp registers and independent testimony.
basis_and_limitations: Hearman, printed pp.82–83 and 91–92; Zainab is a pseudonym interviewed decades later. The policy purpose is Hearman’s reconstruction, supported by cited military material; no evacuation order, camp roster, ration register or field-hospital log was directly inspected. S1310 and S1324 are the same author’s overlapping research program.
next_verification: Find the cited military operation pages, Zainab interview record if access permits, village evacuation lists, Bakung camp registers, ration/medical logs and testimony from other camps and villages.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that Zainab, a pseudonymous South Blitar resident, returned after evacuation to find rice, a goat and chickens missing from her household; she attributed this to military occupation of the home.
claim_type: Pseudonymous retrospective oral testimony reproduced in a scholarly article
confidence: High that Hearman reports the testimony; medium for the individual household loss and its actor attribution without an inventory or independent witness.
basis_and_limitations: Printed p.92. This is one household account and does not quantify looting or establish uniform military conduct across villages. The original interview has not been reviewed.
next_verification: Locate interview notes/audio, household and village records, and testimony from neighboring families; identify the unit present in the area during the relevant period.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that Zainab had to report daily to authorities for several months after returning and cook or perform household chores for soldiers posted in her village.
claim_type: Pseudonymous retrospective oral testimony reproduced in a scholarly article
confidence: High that Hearman reports the account; medium for the duration and routine pending independent testimony or reporting records.
basis_and_limitations: Printed p.92. The interview account is retrospective and identifies Zainab by pseudonym; no reporting cards, village orders, duty rosters or officer identities were inspected.
next_verification: Find the interview source and village daily-report records, identify the local military post and compare other residents’ accounts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman interprets the New Order’s response to South Blitar crop projects as a contest over rural political legitimacy and argues that the PKI was unlikely to have been a de facto government because she estimates the fugitive cadre population at no more than about 150.
confidence: High that Hearman advances this interpretation; low-to-moderate for the fugitive headcount and causal weight absent rosters and policy records.
basis_and_limitations: Printed pp.90–91. Her under-150 figure is an estimate, not a verified census. The legitimacy interpretation is the author’s analysis; it neither establishes that the PKI projects had broad control nor resolves their material effects.
next_verification: Find village and party rosters, military assessments and local administrative records; compare resource allocation, support, coercion, food access and state policies without treating the author’s interpretation as a final political judgment.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Komnas HAM’s Ad Hoc team says it worked from 1 June 2008 to 30 April 2012, examined 349 witnesses/victims and visited some regions, but could not investigate every region or hear every related witness because the events covered a vast geography and the team lacked sufficient budget and faced the passage of time.
claim_type: Official retrospective investigation’s own methodology and limitation statement
confidence: High for the report’s stated mandate, count and limitations; not a representative sample of national victims.
basis_and_limitations: Executive summary printed pp.2–3, directly checked in Indonesian. The 349 is the number of examined witness/victim statements, not an estimate of the total affected population. The underlying BAPs, sampling rules and full item-level geography were not inspected.
next_verification: Obtain the full investigation report and accessible BAPs; map interview location and event location separately; establish how names, duplicates, ethnicity and violation categories were recorded.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Komnas HAM’s executive summary describes October 1965 terror in Makassar against PKI members or people considered PKI-related and also ethnic Chinese who were identified with the PRC; it provides no national count or victim-ethnicity percentage for this episode.
period: 1965-10; Makassar and surrounding area; report published 2012
claim_type: Official retrospective account based on witness evidence; regional scope
confidence: High that the report states this; medium for individual incidents pending underlying witness BAPs and local records.
basis_and_limitations: The report’s regional narrative identifies a perceived association with the PRC, not proof that all ethnic Chinese shared a political affiliation. Search of the report found no national ethnicity-coded victim table; its local narrative cannot establish national proportions.
next_verification: Read the relevant witness BAPs and Makassar command, police, detention, property and burial records; identify victims by person and self-identified/community identity without inferring affiliation from ethnicity.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that a pseudonymous woman, Suginem, was widowed during the South Blitar operation and was forced by a soldier deployed to her village who later served as village head to meet his sexual demands; the article says her child became severely malnourished.
period: 1968; South Blitar after the Trisula operation
claim_type: Pseudonymous retrospective oral testimony reproduced in a scholarly article
confidence: High that Hearman reports the account; medium for individual circumstances pending the original interview and independent records.
basis_and_limitations: Printed pp.92–93 and note 63. Suginem is a pseudonym. The article provides a later oral-history account; no original interview, medical record, complaint, appointment order or village register was inspected. This is an individual reported case, not evidence of uniform conduct by every soldier or village head.
next_verification: Locate the interview notes/audio and consent metadata; identify the appointed village head and unit from local records; seek family testimony, medical and village records and independent reports of sexual coercion.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Liem reports, citing the Brawijaya military history, that the military replaced village administrators in South Blitar with 234 ABRI caretakers as part of efforts to weaken local support for the underground and collect information.
claim_type: Later oral-history chapter quoting an official military history
confidence: High that Liem reports the figure and cited source; medium-to-low for the exact number, period and full replacement coverage without the roster.
basis_and_limitations: Liem, printed p.182 and note 17, cites Kodam VIII/Brawijaya, Operasi Trisula, p.243. The military book and its 234-name list have not been directly opened. A registered count does not prove that all appointments were implemented simultaneously or in every village.
next_verification: Obtain Operasi Trisula p.243 and the underlying caretaker roster; compare appointment dates, villages, prior pamong, military posts, and village administrative records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Farmer Ruslan recalled that his village-head uncle ordered him and other local men to carry packs and supplies for an Army group of about forty soldiers while it walked between Tumpakoyot, Ngrejo, Bakung and Sumberdadi to map the area.
period: Before Trisula; South Blitar, exact date unspecified
claim_type: Retrospective civilian oral testimony about compelled military logistics and reconnaissance
confidence: High that Liem records this account; medium for troop size, route and exact purpose.
basis_and_limitations: Liem, printed p.182, separately describes the movement as an Army survey/mapping trip and records Ruslan’s “if I am not mistaken” estimate of forty soldiers. No patrol diary, map, requisition slip or village order was obtained; the named route points and district boundaries require verification.
next_verification: Find Ruslan’s interview recording/transcript, village-head records, military patrol maps and route journals; identify the date/unit and compare other residents’ accounts of carrying, provisioning and intelligence mapping.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Rewang retrospectively blamed impatience and “shortcuts” among some PKI leaders for premature armed activity: he said unfinished, dispersed shelters and party work were overtaken by local weapons seizures and attacks, which alerted military authorities and preceded encirclement and defeat.
confidence: High that Rewang makes this analysis; medium-to-low as a complete causal explanation of the underground’s defeat.
basis_and_limitations: Liem, printed pp.179–181, records Rewang discussing Vietnam-inspired long-term organization, “shortcuts,” arms seizure and the resulting military operation. This account is retrospective and comes from one former leader; it does not establish that every cadre agreed, that every raid caused discovery, or that organizational weakness alone explains defeat. Compare with local actions, military intelligence, capture records and broader repression.
next_verification: Find the cited Rewang memoir and original interview, dated weapons seizures and attacks, military intelligence/encirclement orders, captured correspondence and independent villagers’ accounts; weigh the leadership critique against state force, local support and operational constraints.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The reported number of ABRI caretaker village officials in South Blitar in 1968 differs by source: Liem cites 234 registered caretakers from the 1969 Brawijaya history, while the 1978 government history reports 144, citing a 1975 Blitar regency booklet.
claim_type: Cross-source discrepancy in retrospective official counts
confidence: High that the two publications give these figures; low-to-medium that they count the same territory, posts and date range.
basis_and_limitations: Liem, printed p.182 note 17, cites Semdam VIII/Brawijaya, Operasi Trisula, p.243 for 234. Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur, printed p.269 note 574, cites Pemkab Blitar, Selayang Pandang Blitar Selatan (1975), p.1 for 144. Neither underlying roster/booklet was obtained; the figures may differ by date, geographic scope or definition, or one may be wrong.
next_verification: Obtain both cited books and appointment registers; identify dates, villages, caretaker roles, totals by subdistrict, and whether the number is people appointed, positions filled or cumulative replacements.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1978 East Java history reports that a civil territorial-development post was established in Bakung on 20 May 1968 under Blitar regent Sanoesi Prawirodihardjo, with a “3P” remit: education, food and infrastructure.
claim_type: Government-sponsored history citing a local regency publication
confidence: High that the 1978 book reports this date, chair and remit; medium for the original order and actual implementation.
basis_and_limitations: Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur, printed p.269, note 574 cites Pemkab Blitar, Selayang Pandang Blitar Selatan (1975), p.1. That booklet, appointment order, budget and daily reports were not obtained. The post was part of a stated civil-territorial program conducted alongside intelligence operations, not proof that all services were delivered as described.
next_verification: Obtain the 1975 booklet and the Bakung post’s founding order, staffing roster, supply/budget records, monthly reports and village-level implementation files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur (1978) dates the start of Operation Trisula to 31 May 1968 and says it lasted about two months; it then distinguishes territorial rehabilitation/stabilization through 7 September from civil territorial guidance through 16 December 1968.
claim_type: Official retrospective chronology with named military and local source citations
confidence: High that the 1978 book states these phases; medium for their exact operational boundaries and coverage.
basis_and_limitations: Printed p.269 dates Trisula to 31 May; p.270 describes an approximately two-month operation, then a territorial phase through 7 September and a civil-territorial phase through 16 December. Hearman describes the named counterinsurgency as beginning in June and formally ending 7 September; Leksana cites 31 May for the task-force launch. These labels may describe formation, combat, territorial consolidation and formal closure; no authenticated order set or after-action calendar has resolved the stages.
next_verification: Inspect the 1969 Semdam history, order and phase logs, 1973 presidential accountability address, Trisula monument inscription and local posts’ diaries; distinguish task-force formation, first combat, “physical” phase, handover and ceremonial closure.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1978 official history describes South Blitar as the East Java underground’s strongest and best-armed Kompro, claims it had many ABRI fugitives/escapees, says two Detga and 17 Gerda were organized by early 1968, and attributes STPR/KKPR training in South Malang with cadres circulated across East Java.
claim_type: Official retrospective account relaying military-history claims
confidence: High that the 1978 book makes these claims; low-to-medium for actual strength, armament, school operation and numbers.
basis_and_limitations: Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur, printed pp.266–267 notes 566–567 cites Semdam VIII/Brawijaya, Operasi Trisula, pp.5 and 8–11. It calls the Kompro strongest and sufficiently armed; Rewang and Muyatno’s later accounts to Liem and Munir’s 1973 defense instead describe dispersed, underprepared formations and say no regular TPR existed. Those statements concern different organizational categories and vantage points; no authenticated roster, weapon inventory, course register or school record is available.
next_verification: Obtain the cited military-history pages, captured Kompro documents, original Perjuta/training manuals, Detga/Gerda rosters, weapons inventory, training attendance and independent accounts from local recruits and residents.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1978 history reports that Brawijaya commander M. Jasin said at a Malang press conference on 9 August 1968 that 850 people classified as PKI detainees had been detained by then and that 37 firearms and four grenades had been seized.
claim_type: Retrospective government history quoting a commander’s press-conference report
confidence: High that the 1978 book reports these numbers; medium-to-low for the underlying count, classification and completeness.
basis_and_limitations: Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur, printed p.270 note 576 cites M. Jasin’s 9 August 1968 press conference as printed in the third edition of Sketsmasa, Operasi Trisula, p.14. The pamphlet, press transcript, detainee register and seizure ledger remain uninspected. “850 detainees” is not a death toll or a complete final operation total.
next_verification: Obtain Sketsmasa p.14 and the original press transcript; compare the figure with custody registers, camp lists, release/transfer/death records and the itemized seizure ledger.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1978 history claims that South Blitar residents “practically sided” with the PKI and were instructed to use a “GTM/T-3” response—“do not know, do not know [the person], do not understand”—when questioned by government officials.
claim_type: Official military-political allegation reproduced in a government history
confidence: High that the book makes the allegation; low-to-medium that this represented an organized instruction across the population.
basis_and_limitations: Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur, printed p.267 note 568 cites Jasin’s 9 August press-conference account as reproduced in Sketsmasa’s 1969 third edition, pp.12–13. No text of the alleged instruction, distribution list, military interrogation records, or village-level testimony verifying its breadth was obtained. Liem reports residents providing warnings/support in some cases and a farmer compelled to carry military supplies in another; neither set can represent all residents.
next_verification: Obtain the conference transcript and pamphlet pages; search captured papers for GTM/T-3 instructions and compare with independent interviews, interrogation transcripts and village records from different sites.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1978 government history categorizes South Blitar Kompro activity as “armed propaganda” and alleges robbery, kidnapping and retaliatory killings in Blitar and Tulungagung.
claim_type: Official military-history allegation repeated in a retrospective government history
confidence: High that the 1978 book reports the allegation; low-to-medium on incident-by-incident attribution, authorization and casualty details.
basis_and_limitations: Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur, printed p.267 note 569 cites Semdam VIII/Brawijaya, Operasi Trisula, pp.8–11. Rewang later described some attacks and disarmament as local actions beyond Kompro authorization; Munir’s legal defense characterized named 1968 encounters as compelled self-defense. Neither the military account nor those retrospective statements provide a complete incident ledger.
next_verification: Identify incidents, dates, victims, suspects, weapons and command links from the military book, police/district reports, court files, local burial records, detainee testimony and party correspondence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1978 history cites a “Pedoman Aksi Kota” attributed to Datong Sugiarto and others and dated 10 November 1968 as evidence of a planned mass disruption in Surabaya for March 1968.
claim_type: Retrospective source chronology anomaly / official allegation
confidence: High that the 1978 book makes this claim; low that the later-dated document proves a March plan existed before Trisula.
basis_and_limitations: Sejarah Daerah Jawa Timur, printed pp.267–268 says the mass action was planned for March 1968, but describes the cited document as made on 10 November 1968; note 570 points to Sketsmasa’s 1969 third edition, p.34. The underlying document and pamphlet page are not available. Unless the date or characterization is wrong, the source postdates the alleged plan and cannot establish what authorities knew before the May–June operation.
next_verification: Obtain the original “Pedoman Aksi Kota,” the 1969 pamphlet p.34 and any capture/interrogation report; authenticate authorship, document date, intended action date, provenance and whether the plan was retrospective or misdated.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The December 1968 CIA study reconstructs the first planning meeting on 6 September 1965 at Captain Wahjudi’s home: it says Sjam introduced the Generals’ Council threat and proposed a new government/Revolutionary Council, while the officers asked how the Council would be formed and who would lead it.
claim_type: Retrospective intelligence reconstruction based on participant interrogations
confidence: High that the CIA report gives this account; low-to-moderate for the actual meeting details and their completeness.
basis_and_limitations: CIA study printed pp.109–113, especially its account of 4 Sep contact and 6 Sep meeting. The foreword states that its account of the conspiracy derives entirely from interrogations of participants; no authenticated meeting notes, participant’s contemporary diary or complete uncoerced transcript was checked. The CIA’s account does not establish that the full Politburo or PKI Central Committee authorized the operation.
next_verification: Obtain the cited Latief/Untung/Wahjudi interrogation and trial records, compare their wording and timing, search Sjam/Pono and military correspondence, and seek any surviving Central Committee or Special Bureau minutes.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1968 CIA study reports that Subandrio’s interrogation record attributed to Zhou Enlai a January 1965 offer of 100,000 free light arms for a proposed “Fifth Force”; it also says Omar Dani’s mid-September Beijing mission concerned final arrangements, but explicitly states that the arms-to-G30S connection is unclear.
claim_type: Intelligence report about an alleged foreign arms offer and negotiations
confidence: High that the CIA report makes and qualifies this claim; low-to-moderate for the offer/near-final deal as described because the cited Indonesian statement is an interrogation record and direct Chinese approvals, transport and receipts remain absent.
basis_and_limitations: CIA study printed pp.130–131 and note to p.131 attributes the offer to Subandrio’s interrogation report; it says Dani returned from Beijing on 19 Sep after a secret trip and reports discussion of 100,000 arms. Zhou’s separate study (S134; C118–C119), citing Chinese MFA records and interviews, distinguishes offer, Indonesian Air Force request for 25,000, negotiations and the absence of proof that the large shipment arrived before G30S. Neither study establishes weapon-by-weapon receipt or use.
next_verification: Obtain Subandrio and Dani trial/interrogation records, the 17 Sep Zhou–Dani minutes if released, Indonesian Air Force request/receipt files, Chinese authorization, aircraft/ship manifests, customs or airfield records, serial numbers and receiving-unit ledgers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A 30 November 1965 U.S. Embassy cable reports that Polish First Secretary Andrzej Gradziuk attributed to an unnamed PKI Central Committee contact the claim that only a small group headed by Aidit knew of the September 30 plan and that its idea originated outside the PKI, possibly with Sukarno.
period: 1965-10-01 account reported to U.S. Embassy on 1965-11-30
claim_type: Contemporaneous diplomatic report of layered hearsay
confidence: High that the Embassy cable records this report; low for the underlying statement and source attribution.
basis_and_limitations: RG 84, Entry P 339, Box 14, Folder 7; scan pages 1–3 visually checked. The alleged PKI source is unnamed, the cable does not provide a signed statement or interview transcript, and the Polish diplomat is reporting an account to U.S. Embassy staff. The U.S. reporting officer explicitly raises possible fabrication.
next_verification: Seek the Polish Embassy’s original notes and Ministry of Foreign Affairs dispatches, identify the PKI contact if possible, and compare with Aidit/Sjam/Politburo records, participant testimony and contemporaneous party communications.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the same reported account, the unnamed PKI contact allegedly said participants agreed to a limited operation to seize selected generals without killing them and expected Sukarno to make a public statement on 1 October.
confidence: High that the cable records the claim; low that it accurately represents the planners’ actual collective intention.
basis_and_limitations: The account passes from an unnamed PKI CC contact to Polish First Secretary Gradziuk and then to the U.S. Embassy; the Embassy explicitly says the account may have been doctored. It conflicts in form with public actions and later interrogation accounts but cannot be resolved by treating either public statement or interrogation as transparent access to private intent.
next_verification: Find the Polish source notes and compare against the exact movement orders, operational plans, records for the capture teams, contemporaneous statements and uncoerced participant accounts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The U.S. Embassy author of Telegram 1025 A explicitly considered that Gradziuk’s account might have been “doctored” and noted uncertainty about whether it nevertheless contained useful information.
confidence: High for the wording and existence of the caveat in the scanned cable.
basis_and_limitations: The last page of the linked telegram includes the author’s comment that the story may have been designed to solicit Embassy opinion and that the source may have been fabricated, while also noting the diplomat’s prior relationship with the source. This is the U.S. officer’s assessment, not independent proof either that the story was true or that it was doctored.
next_verification: Identify the Embassy drafter and the cited contact history; search Polish, Soviet and Indonesian records for independent documentation of the same account.

atomic_claim_or_observation: John Roosa reports that Abdul Latief later testified that he signed the 25 October 1965 military-police interrogation record while severely wounded, medicated, immobilized and barely conscious after capture.
claim_type: Scholarly report of a defendant’s later statement about interrogation conditions
confidence: High that Roosa reports the later testimony and cites the relevant records; moderate for the precise conditions pending direct review of the original BAP and trial file.
basis_and_limitations: Roosa, Indonesia no.85, pp.46–48 and notes 53–58; he says he had a copy of the 25 Oct military-police BAP and cites Latief’s 1978 testimony and 2000 printed plea. The 1965 BAP, complete 1978 court record and medical/custody records were not independently accessed in this pass.
next_verification: Retrieve the original BAP, 1978 hearing transcript, Latief plea, injury/medical and custody records, and the 21/23 Dec 1965 follow-up interrogations.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Roosa says that Latief’s 21 and 23 December 1965 follow-up interrogation records reversed the October 25 statement: Latief denied PKI affiliation and denied that the PKI led the September 30 Movement; Roosa says the New Order official account did not cite those later records.
claim_type: Scholarly comparison of contradictory interrogation records
confidence: High that Roosa reports the contradiction and that the 1968 CIA study foregrounds the earlier interrogation-based narrative; moderate for the precise contents pending direct comparison of all records.
basis_and_limitations: Roosa, pp.46–49, notes 58–68, cites KOPKAMTIB Team Pemeriksa Pusat records dated 21 and 23 Dec 1965; the original records were not opened. The CIA study was published before those records’ evidentiary history was resolved and states its planning account rests on interrogations. The differing statements cannot be adjudicated without originals and custody context.
next_verification: Obtain both December records, compare them line by line with 25 Oct and public 1978 testimony; inspect publication citations and trial exhibits to establish which versions were used, omitted or challenged.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that some South Blitar fugitives organized three-person cells with separate responsibility for organization, education/outreach, and armed struggle; Tuti worked in a cell’s outreach role seeking former party members and supporters.
claim_type: Scholarly reconstruction of underground cell organization
confidence: High that the article records these interview accounts; moderate for the cell structure’s extent and the division’s consistency across the base.
basis_and_limitations: Hearman, printed pp.80–81 and notes 100–102, draws on interviews with Winata and Tuti. The third cell member and a contemporaneous roster are not identified; the article says exact activities are difficult to reconstruct beyond regrouping supporters.
next_verification: Obtain the original ISSI interview recordings/transcripts, underground contact reports and any surviving cell rosters.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Hearman reports that the South Blitar network prepared limited weapons-handling training; a military operation history she cites says two captured youth detachments yielded 34 firearms, some old, and several blowpipes, and Hearman assesses the armed capacity as embryonic and short of trainers, weapons and ammunition.
claim_type: Scholarly report citing a New Order military operational history
confidence: High that Hearman reports the number and her assessment; low-to-moderate as a complete inventory of weapons or training across South Blitar.
basis_and_limitations: Hearman, pp.80–81 and notes 103–106, cites the 1969 Brawijaya history pp.27, 34. The military inventory is a report by the operation’s own institution; no complete seizure ledger or independent arms survey was inspected. “34” should not be treated as a comprehensive PKI inventory.
next_verification: Obtain Operasi Trisula pp.27 and 34, original seizure records, serials, custody logs, training rosters and local arms procurement evidence.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In a 1973 defense statement, PKI leader Mohammad Munir attributed the South Blitar defeat partly to rushing to rebuild the party and exposing its presence before preparations for battle were mature.
claim_type: Participant’s later courtroom explanation quoted by a scholar
confidence: High that Hearman quotes this argument; moderate-to-low as a complete causal explanation of the defeat.
basis_and_limitations: Hearman, printed p.82, quotes Munir’s 1973 defense statement. It is a participant’s retrospective and legal argument; no complete original speech, command minutes or independent operational timeline was checked.
next_verification: Retrieve Munir’s full 1973 defense statement and compare its account with Rewang’s interviews, local attack records, arrests, informant reports and the military’s chronology.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Ian Baird’s 2025 article describes the Communist Party of Thailand’s 1961 shift toward rural work and covert base preparation, followed by armed fighting in 1965 and development of northern strongholds by 1967–68, with Hmong and Lua communities joining in those highland areas.
claim_type: Peer-reviewed secondary chronology with oral-history and ethnographic framing
confidence: High that the article states this sequence; moderate for exact national chronology and the size/representativeness of minority recruitment.
basis_and_limitations: Baird’s article cites prior histories for the strategic and military chronology and is centered on a later 1970s Hmong/Lua history project and one veteran’s account. The first-clash date conflicts with sources giving 7 August rather than 8 August 1965; CPT records were not inspected.
next_verification: Compare the article’s cited 1961/1965 records with Thai regional military reports, CPT histories, PLAT records, Voice of the People of Thailand broadcasts and Hmong/Lua community histories.

atomic_claim_or_observation: An FCO 168/2193 chart reproduced as a one-page scan depicts the SEAMU coordinator’s link to political, diplomatic and psychological-warfare offices; it lists a black Indonesian newsletter, Indonesia research, PSYOPS services, contacts and weekly meetings between intelligence collectors and users as stated functions or working methods.
period: British information operations, mid-1960s; chart undated
claim_type: Contemporary institutional diagram in later archival reproduction
confidence: High for the labels and organizational relationships visible on the chart; low for whether every stated meeting or function was carried out in practice.
basis_and_limitations: The chart lists counter-Confrontation exploitation of diplomatic information, guidance to SEAMU/PSYOPS, liaison with British missions, and collector/user roles; the reproduced image gives 1965/1966 budget estimates excluding salaries. It is not a meeting log, distribution list or activity return, and the original TNA file was not directly retrieved.
next_verification: Request the full FCO 168/2193 file and meeting minutes, staffing/payroll, tasking papers, station reports, newsletter dispatch receipts and PSYOPS activity logs.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Telegram 1863 of 8 October 1965 assigned the Information Research Department responsibility for proposed overt outlets, said separate instructions would cover the clandestine “black” channel, and asked “Peck” to consult Kuala Lumpur/BGRAI about how far suitable Malaysians should be brought into confidence.
confidence: High for the telegram’s instructions; no evidence in this source that Malaysian personnel agreed or acted.
basis_and_limitations: FCO 168/1668, pp.1–2, visually checked. The document outlines internal tasking, not an executed media schedule or confirmed Malaysian participation; the scan is hosted by a documentary reproduction site.
next_verification: Locate the separately referenced black-channel instructions, Peck’s meeting notes, KL/BGRAI files, broadcast logs and any receipt or posting records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sudisman’s September 1966 Politburo self-criticism says the Party had not achieved a shared decision about the principal form of struggle; the issue remained with a small leadership/cadre circle, leaving most Party members passive on a strategic question.
confidence: High that the reproduced text makes this diagnosis; moderate-to-low as an independently verified account of all internal deliberations.
basis_and_limitations: “Pokok-pokok kelemahan” section; Indonesian text and selected pages of the 1971 collection checked. The text does not name all participants or establish what each leader privately believed.
next_verification: Find Politburo/CC minutes, draft versions, cadre-school papers, provincial reports and correspondence on armed strategy; compare with Sudisman’s 1967 defense, Supardjo’s report and oral histories.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The same self-criticism says some party leaders used separate political and organizational channels outside Politburo/CC control; competent collective bodies sometimes approved steps already taken and did so with incomplete information.
period: PKI organization before September 1965; assessment written September 1966
claim_type: Internal party diagnosis of decision procedures
confidence: High that the document says this; moderate as a description of scope and frequency, since no decision register or named cases accompanies the general charge.
basis_and_limitations: “Pokok-pokok kesalahan organisasi” section, selected reprint pages checked. The text does not identify which channels or actions it means; it cannot by itself prove that a particular G30S order bypassed a specified body.
next_verification: Identify named decisions, channels and participants in original CC/Politburo records; compare C393, C2317–C2318, C2400 and G30S trial/interrogation files.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The September 1966 text criticizes PKI’s long reliance on legal-parliamentary activity as its principal path and says the Party did not prepare members and mass organizations for a violent counterattack; it treats the post-1951 emphasis on legality as organizational vulnerability.
claim_type: Internal party strategic and organizational self-criticism
confidence: High that the self-criticism states this; low-to-moderate as a complete causal explanation of the Party’s collapse. Sudisman’s 1967 courtroom statement separately denies that the Party as an institution decided G30S, so the two documents must be compared in their different settings.
basis_and_limitations: Text sections on the peaceful/parliamentary path and organizational legalism, reprint pages checked; compare Sudisman’s detained-defendant speech. The statement does not establish that legal mass work was inherently a mistake or that earlier arms preparation could have defeated the Army.
next_verification: Compare PKI statutes/congress resolutions, 1956/1959/1962/1965 records, provincial security plans, army repression plans, mass-organization instruction and internal debate before/after 1 October.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The 1966 self-criticism says rapid membership expansion was prioritized beyond the Party’s capacity to educate and supervise new members; it repeats a Party figure of more than three million members and says cadre development drew senior organizers toward state/semi-state posts and away from rural work.
claim_type: Internal party organizational self-criticism; membership figure is the document’s own reported figure
confidence: High that the document reports these points; moderate-to-low for the exact membership count and national representativeness because no audited roll is supplied.
basis_and_limitations: The text contrasts membership plan targets and cadre training and says village cadres were drawn toward cities/central offices. These are politically charged post-defeat diagnoses by surviving leaders, not a membership census or independent employment survey.
next_verification: Obtain annual member rolls and branch returns, party-plan reports, cadre placement lists, education records, organizational statutes and provincial mass-organization records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The September 1966 program calls for the party to operate wholly clandestinely, rebuild rural bases and prepare armed peasant struggle; this marks the surviving leadership’s post-defeat program and should not be projected backward as proof that the pre-1965 legal PKI already had an operational guerrilla plan.
confidence: High for the program’s stated direction; low for how far it was implemented nationally. South Blitar’s later cell, arms and authorization evidence remains localized and contested.
basis_and_limitations: “Jalan Keluar” section; compare pre-G30S party practice and later South Blitar interviews. Do not infer from ideological declaration that countrywide armed structures existed.
next_verification: Find distribution/circulation records for the 1966 document, subsequent central/provincial directives and evidence of implementation outside East Java.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A CIA-hosted 2016 retrospective article by Bob Bergin distinguishes the Communist Party of Thailand’s 1952 declared commitment to armed struggle from the onset of an insurgency in 1965; Baird’s 2025 account separately describes a 1961 shift toward covert rural organizing and base preparation. These are distinct stages, not necessarily contradictory dates.
confidence: High that the two articles present these stages; moderate for the precise chronology pending CPT congress records and contemporaneous Thai incident files.
basis_and_limitations: Bergin, Studies in Intelligence 60(2), pp.25–26, says doctrine commitment 1952 but insurgency began 1965; Baird gives the post-1961 rural transition. Neither opened a CPT congress minute or complete operational log.
next_verification: Retrieve CPT congress resolutions and regional instructions, and Thai police/military incident records for 1961–65; distinguish strategic declaration, cadre deployment, first clash and sustained insurgency.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Bergin’s 2016 article reports, citing a former senior Thai intelligence official, that CPT membership probably did not exceed about 2,500 at its peak and that the organization used small, highly secretive cells with much of its leadership hidden in the jungle or China.
claim_type: Retrospective security-service estimate and organizational assessment
confidence: High that Bergin reports this estimate and description; low-to-moderate for the number and its definition because it is not based on a published roster and “member” is not defined.
basis_and_limitations: Bergin pp.26–27 relies on interviews with former Thai intelligence leaders and cites the party’s secrecy as a collection difficulty. Do not compare the number directly with PKI mass membership, armed combatants or the U.S. 1968 NIE categories.
next_verification: Find CPT membership estimates by year, internal cadre/branch records, Thai arrest and defector rosters and independent regional oral histories.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Bergin reports that Chinese support to the CPT included some finance, arms and ammunition, leadership training in Beijing and VOPT broadcasts said by Thai intelligence to originate in Kunming; the same account describes the CPT as substantially self-financed and dependent on captured arms.
confidence: High that the article reports these claims; moderate-to-low for the specific aid quantities, timing and broadcast-site attribution pending Chinese and CPT records.
basis_and_limitations: The passage quotes a former Thai intelligence official; its VOPT-location note refers to Thai government direction-finding and an NIA interview. This is a comparator for channel types, not evidence about assistance to Indonesia.
next_verification: Check Chinese party/diplomatic archives, VOPT program recordings and transmitter logs, CPT supply accounts and Thai direction-finding/intercept records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Keppres No.48/1962 established nationwide civil defense as a non-military component of national defense and placed central planning/coordination under the Minister of National Security; it directed central and regional governments to mobilize national resources.
confidence: High for the statute’s text and dates; no inference about a particular 1965 unit or course.
basis_and_limitations: Keppres 48, operative clauses 1–4, PDF pp.1–2. It created a general framework, not a Fifth Force or named Lubang Buaya program.
next_verification: Compare with implementing regulations, district orders, budgets and local civil-defense registers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Keppres No.128/1962 assigned central planning, implementation, coordination, control and supervision of civil defense and popular resistance to the First Deputy Minister for Defense/Security, with regional activity governed under that authority.
confidence: High for the decree’s delegation; actual local implementation unverified.
basis_and_limitations: Keppres 128, clauses 1–4. The decree also references the general mobilization regulation PERPU 1/1962.
next_verification: Locate regulations issued under the decree and any 1965 AURI/base-specific delegation.

atomic_claim_or_observation: UU No.14/1962 made general mobilization a presidential/Supreme Commander decision after hearing the National Defense Council and stated that organized, trained popular resistance could assist armed forces and perform civil-defense duties.
period: Law enacted 6 Sep 1962; effective retroactively 19 Dec 1961
confidence: High for statutory wording; the text does not establish that general mobilization was declared or that a particular course was authorized.
basis_and_limitations: UU 14/1962, arts.1–2, PDF pp.3–4; BPK metadata.
next_verification: Find any presidential mobilization declaration, call-up notices, implementing regulations and 1965 course authorization.

atomic_claim_or_observation: UU No.14/1962 allowed healthy Indonesian citizens of either sex aged 18–50 to be summoned for active popular resistance, assistance to armed forces, civil-defense duties and related training.
confidence: High for text; low for any claim that a given person was called or trained under it.
next_verification: Find actual call-up, health screening, training and exemption records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The reviewed 1962 legal texts establish general civil-defense/popular-resistance and mobilization mechanisms but do not name an “Angkatan Kelima” service or authorize the specific Lubang Buaya/HANREV course by name.
confidence: High for the reviewed text; it is not evidence that no separate 1965 order or instruction existed.
basis_and_limitations: Read the full three legal instruments; they distinguish general legal authority from a particular policy proposal or operational order.
next_verification: Find specific 1965 AURI orders, legal opinions and Fifth Force command/organization papers.

atomic_claim_or_observation: A 1994 Sekretariat Negara history, available here only through a blog transcription, asserts that Omar Dhani issued a 10 March 1965 instruction to establish Hansip at each air-base command and that Sujono sent coded radiograms to Korud battalions directing training teams and priority for labor/farmer organizations.
confidence: High that the accessible transcription makes this assertion; low that the original order and radiograms said or did this because none were obtained.
basis_and_limitations: Chapter IV transcription, paragraphs beginning “Pelatihan Kemiliteran PKI...” and quoted radio-order text. It is not the March instruction or radio record itself.
next_verification: Retrieve the signed 10 March instruction, coded radio text, sender/receiver logs, Korud acknowledgements and base training reports.

atomic_claim_or_observation: The same 1994 narrative says plans to train at Kalijati, Tasikmalaya and Semplak/Bogor were blocked by Koramil reactions and that Sujono therefore concentrated Hansip training at Lubang Buaya.
claim_type: Retrospective official narrative about inter-service/local response
confidence: High that the narrative reports this; low for the claimed Koramil actions and causal reason without contemporaneous records.
basis_and_limitations: Same Chapter IV transcription, paragraph on proposed bases and centralization. The military-trial testimony reviewed here does not independently confirm this specific sequence.
next_verification: Search local Koramil/Kodim correspondence, AURI base plans, cancelled course registers and Sujono’s original statements.

atomic_claim_or_observation: In the 16 Feb 1966 Mahmillub testimony, former Major Sujono said he took the initiative to hold training at Lubang Buaya under an earlier Deputy Minister of Operations instruction to add Hansip personnel to air-base defenses and in light of Omar Dhani’s public statements; he also acknowledged there was no formal written order for the initiative.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom testimony about command/authorization chain
confidence: High that the published court record reproduces this testimony; moderate-to-low for the complete underlying command chain because the written order is absent and the witness was detained.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.204–207. The text itself distinguishes a prior instruction, ministerial statements and Sujono’s own initiative; do not collapse them into one signed command.
next_verification: Locate Sri Mulyono Herlambang and Omar Dhani orders, AURI command logs, Sujono’s detention/interrogation file and testimony in another case.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sujono testified that BTI and SERBAUD and other mass organizations requested training, that he called them together and agreed to begin the first cohort on 5 July 1965.
confidence: High that the transcript records the statement; moderate for actual start and organizer scope pending cohort registers and applicant letters.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.206–207. The testimony attributes the account to Sujono, not to a participant roster.
next_verification: Find organizations’ written requests, course-opening report, site diary and attendance lists.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sujono testified that cohort durations were progressively shortened from 12 days to 10, then 7 and finally 5 days as the training cycle advanced.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom testimony about course duration
confidence: High that the transcript records this account; moderate-to-low for each cohort’s exact dates and duration without schedules.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.213–214. The testimony is retrospective and no training calendars were checked.
next_verification: Compare cohort schedules, trainer logs, meal/supply sheets and participant recall.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sujono described the course as including revolutionary/Pancasila ideological instruction, weapons tactics and technology, revolutionary ethics, and intelligence; he said the final 28–30 September arrivals had only about two days, too little for proper training.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom testimony about curriculum and readiness
confidence: High that this is what the transcript records; low-to-moderate for actual attendance, hours, weapons access and competence.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.213–215. The claim does not establish that every trainee received every module or became operationally capable.
next_verification: Find curriculum sheets, trainer assignment lists, firing-range logs, ammunition issues and individual course records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sujono testified that a group of about 1,500 arrived suddenly at Lubang Buaya on 28 September 1965 and said he could not refuse them.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom testimony about a late arrival
confidence: High that this statement appears in the testimony; low-to-moderate for the count and identity of the full group because no nominal list or independent count was found.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.212–213. This refers to a late arriving group, not necessarily all people ever trained at Lubang Buaya.
next_verification: Obtain site entry/meal rolls, transport and organization dispatch records, and independent witness accounts.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Under cross-examination, Sujono said that from 28 September he had only received his representative’s report of “1,000-something” candidates; he said he had not personally seen the whole group and had not set the exact number.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom testimony clarifying information basis
confidence: High that the text records this qualification; low for the actual count. This is a distinct information basis from the approximately 1,500 arrival estimate in the same testimony.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.223–225. The OCR wording is “1.000 sekian”; do not convert it into an exact figure or average it with 1,500/2,000 claims.
next_verification: Check the representative’s identity and report, the other witness’s notes, attendance list and trial page images.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sujono testified that Lubang Buaya trainees had not been formally constituted as an AURI Hansip unit and were supposed to return to their home organizations after training.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom testimony on formal status
confidence: High that the witness made the statement; moderate-to-low for organizational/legal status without AURI establishment orders and unit rolls.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.212–213. A statement about formal unit recognition does not mean no AURI officers controlled the site or supplied resources.
next_verification: Find AURI unit-formation orders, personnel rosters, pay/supply registers and post-course return records.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sujono testified that Captain Suradi provided 100 Garand rifles intended for Hansip use.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom statement about weapon transfer
confidence: High that the testimony says this; low-to-moderate for delivery, count, custody or use because no issue/receipt ledger was examined.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.214–215. The witness describes what he said was received; no serial-number list, armory entry, ammunition issue or return record was found.
next_verification: Search Suradi and Sujono statements, Halim armory books, requisition/receipt/return vouchers and weapon serials.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Sujono testified that organization-appointed intermediaries Kasiman, Nico/Nicolas and Djohar gathered trainees and arranged food, accommodation and transport, while Major Gatot Sukresno represented Sujono at the site and reported arrival information to him.
claim_type: Sworn courtroom testimony about coordination channels
confidence: High that these names and roles appear in the published statement; moderate-to-low for exact spellings, formal roles and all functions pending rosters and correspondence.
basis_and_limitations: S1353, printed pp.212–213 and 223–225. The account separates mass-organization selection, Suradi’s intermediary role and Sujono’s information through Gatot.
next_verification: Find named individuals’ personnel/organization records, correspondence, transport/food logs and Major Gatot’s reports.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Humaidi’s 2008 thesis reports that a first-course report to Omar Dhani categorized five trainees as nationalist, about 2,000 as communist and none from invited religious organizations; it says Omar requested changes in curriculum, time allocation and political balance.
claim_type: Secondary account of Sujono/Omar reports and later defense material
confidence: High that Humaidi reports these figures; low-to-moderate for the count and its meaning because the cited source chain is Katoppo/Omar’s later defense and it is unclear whether these were plans, cumulative participants or graduates.
basis_and_limitations: Humaidi, printed pp.67–68; note the different category and counting basis from Sujono’s late-September courtroom estimate.
next_verification: Obtain the report, Omar Dhani defense pp.240–241, Katoppo pp.29–36 and cohort lists; define whether numbers mean planned, enrolled, attended or graduated.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Humaidi describes the second course (August 1965) as having shifted from Dwikora volunteer training to a PKI-cadre-oriented “Hada Hanrev” course and lists mass-organization representatives and CC PKI figures as organizers/instructors.
claim_type: Secondary interpretation and reported personnel assignments
confidence: High that Humaidi presents this account; low-to-moderate for actual control, political purpose and each person’s role because the key footnote leads to Katoppo rather than course rosters or orders.
basis_and_limitations: Humaidi, printed pp.67–68 and note citing Katoppo 1999, pp.29–36. The course name and political interpretation should be kept separate from actual curriculum and command.
next_verification: Find course roster, lesson plan, instructor appointment and participant records; compare with Sujono testimony and AURI documents.

atomic_claim_or_observation: Humaidi reports that Komodor Dewanto ordered the training closed after an early-September meeting and that implementation occurred on 26 September 1965.
period: Early Sep and 26 Sep 1965; reported in 2008
